nodes.name: Electrodeposition of Cobalt Hydroxide
nodes.procedure: Cobalt hydroxide nanoarray was synthesized through electrodeposition on carbon cloth substrate. The electrodeposition process was conducted to grow densely arranged nanosheets of Co(OH)2 across the carbon cloth surface, forming a uniform nanosheet morphology.

nodes.source_text: Ru-Co(OH)2/CC was synthesized through a two-step procedure of electrodeposition followed by an ion-exchange process

nodes.name: Ion-exchange with Ruthenium Doping
nodes.procedure: The electrodeposited Co(OH)2/CC was subjected to an ion-exchange process using RuCl3 solution at a concentration of 5 mM. During this ion-exchange process, ruthenium ions were incorporated into the cobalt hydroxide structure, doping the material with ruthenium. The cation exchange process preserved the Co(OH)2 nanosheet morphology on the carbon cloth substrate. The resulting Ru-doped Co(OH)2 nanosheet arrays maintained their ultrathin nanosheet structure.

nodes.description: Electrochemical NO3RR performance in alkaline solution with wastewater-relevant nitrate concentration
nodes.source_text: Ru-Co(OH)2/CC achieved a maximum NH3 FE of ~96% at -0.48 V and sustained a high FE across a broad potential window, significantly outperforming Co(OH)2/CC. With increasingly negative applied potentials, Ru-Co(OH)2/CC delivered a high NH3 yield rate of ~56501 μg h⁻¹ cm_geo⁻² with a large NH3 partial current density of -602.8 mA cm_geo⁻² at -0.48 V vs. RHE.

nodes.description: Electrochemical NO3RR performance in alkaline solution with wastewater-relevant nitrate concentration
nodes.source_text: Co(OH)2/CC outperforming Co(OH)2/CC (27857.3 μg h⁻¹ cm_geo⁻²) and Ru/CC (3244.3 μg h⁻¹ cm_geo⁻²). The onset potential and half-cell energy efficiency (EE) of Ru-Co(OH)2/CC were 0.04 V vs. RHE and 30.4%, respectively, both significantly more favorable than those of Co(OH)2/CC (-0.15 V vs. RHE and 24.3%).

nodes.source_text: Ru/CC (3244.3 μg h⁻¹ cm_geo⁻²). The onset potential and half-cell energy efficiency (EE) of Ru-Co(OH)2/CC were 0.04 V vs. RHE and 30.4%, respectively, both significantly more favorable than those of Co(OH)2/CC (-0.15 V vs. RHE and 24.3%) and Ru/CC (-0.08 V vs. RHE and 3.5%).

Unlike 14NH4+, which exhibited three peaks in the 1H NMR spectra, only the characteristic doublet peaks of 15NH4+ were observed when 15NO3- was used as the nitrogen source. This result confirms that NH3 production resulted from NO3- in the electrolyte.

nodes.description: NO3RR performance at different nitrate concentrations
nodes.source_text: Remarkably, Ru-Co(OH)2/CC achieved impressive NH3 FEs of 85.8% and 98.9% in an Ar-saturated 1 M KOH solution containing 10 mM and 100 mM NO3-, respectively.
Such Ru-Co(OH)2/CC exhibited a comparable NH3 yield rate (7279.07 μg h⁻¹ cm_geo⁻²) and FE (88.5%) to that of under the alkaline conditions.

nodes.description: NO3RR performance for wastewater treatment with simulated wastewater
nodes.source_text: Notably, NO3- and NO2- were reduced to levels below the World Health Organization drinking water standards within 70 min, while maintaining the NH3 FE above 90%, demonstrating excellent NO3- wastewater treatment capabilities.

nodes.description: Durability testing through consecutive electrolysis cycles
nodes.source_text: As shown in Fig. 2i, the NH3 yield rates and FEs were consistently maintained over 12 cycles, indicating good stability.

nodes.description: Membrane electrode assembly (MEA) system NO3RR performance at industrial current density
Operando electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) analysis during NO3RR
nodes.source_text: The charge-transfer resistance observed in the Nyquist plots of Ru-Co(OH)2/CC is smaller than that of Co(OH)2/CC under the same bias, indicating that Ru-Co(OH)2/CC exhibits a faster charge transfer rate during the NO3RR. The peak intensities of Ru-Co(OH)2/CC are lower than those of Co(OH)2/CC and shift to much lower frequencies from 0.1 to -0.4 V vs. RHE. This shift confirms that Ru doping not only slows the Heyrovsky step but also inhibits H2 generation, enabling more efficient capture of H* by NO3- for NH3 formation.

nodes.description: Quasi in situ electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy for hydrogen radical detection
nodes.source_text: After electrolysis in Ar-saturated 1 M KOH solution, Ru-Co(OH)2/CC exhibits significantly stronger DMPO–H signals than Co(OH)2/CC, indicating that Ru-Co(OH)2/CC favors water dissociation and promotes the formation of active hydrogen necessary for protonation. Nearly all DMPO–H signals for Ru-Co(OH)2/CC disappeared, suggesting the rapid consumption of hydrogen radicals on Ru-Co(OH)2/CC to enhance NO3RR hydrogenation energetics.

nodes.description: Open-circuit potential (OCP) measurement for NO3- adsorption behavior
nodes.source_text: A significant decrease in the OCP (~50.1 mV) was observed for Ru-Co(OH)2/CC after adding 2000 ppm NO3-, compared to that for Co(OH)2/CC (~0.6 mV), indicating that Ru doping enhances NO3- adsorption on the catalyst.

nodes.description: In situ Raman spectroscopy during NO3RR at various applied potentials
nodes.source_text: For Ru-Co(OH)2/CC, the stretching vibration peak at 527 cm⁻¹, attributed to Co(OH)2, was observed. At -0.2 V vs. RHE, a new peak at 509 cm⁻¹, corresponding to CoO(OH), appeared, suggesting partial oxidation of Co²⁺ to Co³⁺. Additionally, a peak at 1554 cm⁻¹, attributed to the N–O stretch of HNO, emerged as the potential shifted negatively to -0.9 V vs. RHE. The intensity ratio of the peak at 1060 cm⁻¹ and 1554 cm⁻¹ (I_1060/I_1554) for Ru-Co(OH)2/CC was consistently lower than that of Co(OH)2/CC across the potential range of -0.2 to -0.9 V vs. RHE, indicating more efficient conversion of NO3- to the HNO species.

nodes.description: In situ Raman spectroscopy during NO3RR at various applied potentials
nodes.source_text: In contrast, the Raman spectra of Co(OH)2/CC showed no CoO(OH)-related peaks, with the Co(OH)2 peak at 527 cm⁻¹ remaining unchanged across applied potentials.

nodes.description: MEA system NO3RR performance at industrial current density
nodes.source_text: The Ru-Co(OH)2/CC ∥ IrO2/PTF MEA exhibited significantly reduced resistance and achieved an industrial current density of 500 mA cm⁻² at 2.6 V, markedly outperforming the Co(OH)2/CC ∥ IrO2/PTF device (~280 mA cm⁻² at 2.6 V).

nodes.description: MEA system NO3RR performance at optimized current density with flow rate optimization
nodes.source_text: Using the MEA electrolyzer with Ru-Co(OH)2/CC as the cathode, NO3- was converted to NH3 with a FE of 94 ± 6% and a yield rate of 7472 ± 487 μg h⁻¹ cm_geo⁻² at 100 mA cm⁻², demonstrating excellent potential for NH3 production.

The stability of the MEA system was further investigated, and it maintained an average NH3 FE of ~93%, an NH3 yield rate of ~7000 μg h⁻¹ cm_geo⁻², and a voltage of 1.9 V at 100 mA cm⁻² for over 100 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: Density functional theory calculations show that Ru doping shifts occupied electron states closer to Fermi energy level with higher DOS. d-band center shifts from -2.26 eV for Co(OH)2 to -2.12 eV for Ru-Co(OH)2, indicating stronger interactions with intermediates. NO3- adsorption free energy improves from -2.46 eV to -2.95 eV with Ru doping. Rate-determining step shifts from *NO2 to *HNO transformation with reduced energy barrier from 0.78 eV to 0.64 eV. HER energy barrier of 1.29 eV is higher than NO3RR rate-determining step of 0.64 eV, suggesting kinetic preference for NO3- reduction over HER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The d-band centers of Co(OH)2 and Ru-Co(OH)2 were -2.26 and -2.12 eV, respectively. The adsorption free energy of NO3- on Ru-Co(OH)2 was -2.95 eV, compared to -2.46 eV for Co(OH)2. The rate-determining step (RDS) for Co(OH)2 in the NO3RR is the transformation of *NO2 into *NO, with an energy barrier of 0.78 eV. In contrast, Ru doping alters the RDS to the transition from *HNO to *NH2, significantly reducing the energy barrier to 0.64 eV. The energy barrier for the HER step (*H → 1/2 H2) is 1.29 eV, higher than the 0.64 eV for the NO3RR rate-determining step.
